Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal This Criminal Appeal under Section 374(2) Cr.P.C. has been filed by the appellants Ravi Kol S/o Buddhsen Kol and Arun Dwivedi S/o Rajendra Prasad Dwivedi being aggrieved of the judgment dated 07.08.2015 passed by learned 1st Addl. Sessions Judge, Sidhi District Sidhi in Sessions Trial No. 293 of 2009 whereby, the learned 1st Addl. Sessions Judge convicted the appellants and sentenced as under:-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17053 2 CRA-2131-2015 Conviction Imprisonment Fine (if deposited Imprisonment in Under Act details) lieu of Fine Section 363 IPC RI for 03 years each Rs.1000/- each RI for six months each 366 IPC RI for 05 years each Rs.1000/- each RI for six months each 376(2) (g) IPC RI for life each Rs.10,000/- each RI for one year (Substantive Sentences to run concurrently)
2.

As per the prosecution story in short is that on 29.05.2009 prosecutrix who was aged about 16 years was travelling at about 03:30 p.m. from house of her maternal uncle to her own house when on the way at about 04:00 p.m. she met her neighbor Arun Dwivedi and Ravi Kaul who were travelling on a motorcycle.

They asked the prosecutrix as to where she is going, then Ravi Kol took out a bottle of spray from his pant's pocket and sprayed it on her head and mouth, as a result of which she Ravi Kol vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43238237/
1 questioned, then Arun Dwivedi informed her that spray has been put on her, she started feeling dizziness and turned unconscious.

When she gained consciousness,
she was in a train compartment with 02-03 persons sitting in the compartment.
Arun Dwivedi was sitting by her side.
She ran towards the gate of the train then she found that on the platform board, Chopan station is mentioned, at that time, it was 05-06 in the morning.
Her whole body, head and private parts were aching.
Her undergarment was wet.
When she asked Arun Dwivedi, as to where he is taking her, then he said that he is taking her for sale.

When she informed NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:17053 3 CRA-2131-2015 the Police Personnel and the Train Ticket Conductor then Arun Dwivedi said that since she failed in 09th Class, therefore, she is being taken to her sister's place.
Police Personnel scolded Arun Dwivedi as a result of which, when train stopped they got down.
3. At about 10:00 a.m. a train going towards Mudwas came, in which both of them set down.
In the meanwhile, father of Arun called him, then Arun informed him that he kidnapped the prosecutrix and he is bringing her back.

When the train reached at Bhadoura Station at about 02:00 p.m. then Rajendra Dwivedi boarded the train and asked Arun to jump from the rear side otherwise, father and uncle of the prosecutrix may kill him.

Thereafter, when station came, she came to her house, narrated the incident to her mother, sister and others and informed them that when she was in an unconscious condition, her privacy was violated by Arun Dwivedi and Ravi Kol.
4. Report was lodged on 04.06.2009 at Police Station Majholi, registering Case Crime No. 168/2009 under Section 363, 366 & 376/34 of IPC, thereafter, prosecutrix was subjected to medical examination.
Case was investigated, Charge-sheet was filed.
Accused abjured their guilt.
Trial was conducted and appellants have been sentenced.
5. Shri Vikesh Pratap Singh, learned counsel for the appellants submits that theory of spray is unnatural.
It is submitted that, prosecutrix at the time of the incident was major, she had run away with Aurn Dwivedi.
There was a land dispute between the father of prosecutrix and the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17053 4 CRA-2131-2015 family of Arun and therefore, they have been falsely implicated.
In this regard, documents starting from Ex.D-5 to D-10 have been produced in support of this contention.
6. It is further submitted that, in any case, prosecutrix being major, it will be a consensual relationship and there is no evidence of Ravi Kol violating privacy of the victim.
Therefore, it is submitted that for Arun Dwivedi, its a case of consent and for Ravi Kol, its a case of false implication, therefore, both the appellants deserve to be acquitted.

7. Shri Nitin Gupta, learned Public Prosecutor in his turn submits that, appellants have been convicted under Section 376 (2) (g) of the IPC and as per the explanation given below Section 376(2)(g) of IPC, it is evident that, where a woman is raped by one or more or in a group of persons Ravi Kol vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43238237/

It is submitted that, evidence of PW-1 Dr. Sunita Tiwari corroborates the prosecution story and therefore, there being a common intention between Ravi Kol and Arun Dwivedi, acquittal is not called for in regard to anyone of the appellants.
8. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the records.
9. PW-1 Dr. Sunita Tiwari, has stated that she had carried out radiological examination and had found the radiological age of the prosecutrix to be between 16 to 17 years.

She had prepared X-ray report NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17053 5 CRA-2131-2015 (Ex.P-2) which contains her signatures from 'A' to 'A' part and X-ray Plate (Ex.P-3).
10.
A suggestion has been given to her in para-4 of the cross- examination that the age of the prosecutrix was 18 years but she denied that suggestion.
On a suggestion being given in cross-examination she has stated that all the injuries to the private parts of the prosecutrix were caused because of forceful intercourse.
11. This fact has been corroborated by her while giving her findings in regard to internal examination of the prosecutrix.
As per the Doctor, hymen of the prosecutrix was ruptured at 6.00'O Clock position.
There were signs of infections in the hymen, which were reported to be paining on touch.
There were several abrasions on the Labia Minora towards the internal side.
All the injuries sustained on the private pars were caused within 05-06 days, they were caused due to forceful intercourse/rape.
Victim was under acute pain, she had prepared two slides of the vaginal discharge and had handed them over to the Constable after sealing them in proper condition.

12. PW-3 is the victim, prosecutrix, has stated that when she was travelling on road from her maternal uncle's place to visit her home, then she had met Ravi Kol and Arun Dwivedi who had come on a motorcycle.
They asked her, as to where she is going.

When she said that she is going towards her house, then Ravi Kol had taken out a bottle from his pant pocket and had sprayed it on her head and face, as a result NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17053 6 CRA-2131-2015 of this poisonous substance, she is started feeling dizziness and became unconscious.
She had asked Ravi and Arun as to what has been sprayed on her, then Arun stated that, spray was put, then she became unconscious.
When she gained consciousness, she was in a train compartment alongwith Arun.

It is submitted that, prosecutrix had asked the TT who was accompanied with a man in Khakee Uniform for help and then police personnel had scolded Arun and asked him to drop her back to her home, when Arun had said that since she failed in 9th class, she was being taken to her sister's place.
Thereafter, they got down at a Railway Station.

They waited for another train which came at around 10:00, then they were travelling towards the village of the prosecutrix from Chopan,
when at about 02:00 p.m. appellant Arun had received a call from his father and at the instance of his father he had ran away from the train and the prosecutrix cam back to her village.
At the railway station she met with her mother and sister.
She had narrated her woes to them.

13. Though, Shri Vikesh Pratap Sing, learned counsel for appellants submits that there is delay of 04 to 05 days in lodging of the report but, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, this delay Ravi Kol vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43238237/
3 is not fatal.

sentences.text: Looking to the fact that, victim was a young girl of about 16 to 17 years.
She was unmarried.
Her privacy was violated.

She was subjected to brutalities and under such facts and circumstances, in the light of the judgment of Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of State of Punjab NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17053 7 CRA-2131-2015 Vs. Gurmit Singh and others (1996)2 SCC 384, wherein in para-8, Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "The courts cannot over-look the fact that in sexual offences delay in the lodging of the FIR can be due to variety of reasons particularly the reluctance of the prosecutrix or her family members to go to the police and complain about the incident which concerns the reputation of the prosecutrix and the honour of her family.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is only after giving it a cool thought that a complaint of sexual offence is generally lodged.", delay of 04-05 days, in lodging report cannot be said to be fatal to dent the prosecution story, specially when it is corroborated by the medical evidence of PW-1.
14.
Another suggestion given by Shri Vikesh Pratap Singh, is that since there was a dispute in regard to land between the families of Arun and the prosecutrix, therefore, he has been falsely implicated.
However, the fact of the matter is that, prosecutrix was a minor at the time of incident.

This suggestion has been denied by the prosecutrix and she gave her date of birth in para - 10 of her cross-examination as 05.01.1992, where as incident took place on 29.05.2009, therefore,
admittedly, prosectrix was minor at the time of the incident.
15.

Even otherwise, this fact is corroborated by Dr. Sunita Tiwari (PW- 1) on the basis of radiological examination report (Ex.P-2 & P-3), therefore, when these facts are corroborating each other, then it cannot be said that, prosecutrix was major at the time of the incident.

16. Thus, when all these facts are taken into consideration, then NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:17053 8 CRA-2131-2015 statement of prosecutrix (PW-3) having remained unrebutted and there is specific role assigned to Ravi Kol that he was driving a motorcycle.
Arun was his pillion rider.
Motorcycle was stopped seeing the prosecutrix walking on street.
Arun had asked her as to where she is going.
Then, Ravi Kol had taken out a glass bottle from his pant pocket and had sprayed some chemical substance on the head and face of the prosecutrix that turned her unconscious.

Thereafter, a fact that, prosecutrix complained of pain in her private parts, apart from being feeling wetness etc. duly corroborated by the evidence of Dr. Sunita Tiwari (PW-1), violation of her privacy is proved.
She was seen in the company of Arun Dwivedi in the train a fact which has remained unrebutted.

Appellants have not been able to rebut that part of the theory put forth by the prosecutrix that she while being taken back to her home by train, they had got down at Chopan and thereafter, on receiving a call from his father appellant Arun Dwivedi de-boarded the train from a rear gate leaving the prosecutrix alone, is a sufficient circumstance to reflect on the conduct of the appellant Arun Dwivedi.

Prosecutrix was received by her relatives and she had narrated her woes,
she was suffering from body ache and pain in the private parts, there was white fluid present in her undergarments, being all corroborated with the medical evidence of Dr. Sunita Tiwari (PW-1) which is duly corroborated by FSL Report (Ex.P-22) where on slide (Ex.-A) obtained from the vaginal discharge of the prosecutrix sperms were found, commission of rape is confirmed.

Now the issue arises that whether the violator of the privacy was one or two?

However, this issue looses its significance in the backdrop that in terms of the definition of gangrape and the explanation given below Section 376(2)(g) of IPC as it existed at the relevant point of time, the person who acted in furtherance of common intention will also be said to be a person responsible for commission of gangrape.
There is no rebuttal to the fact that Ravi Kol had not put spray on the head and face of the prosecutrix.

There is also no rebuttal that Ravi Kol had not carried Arun Dwivedi on his motorcycle when the incident took place, therefore, by implication Ravi Kol cannot get a clean chit and therefore, when examined in the light of the provisions contained in Section 376(2)(g) of IPC then conviction of both the appellants cannot be said to be unsustainable or suffering from any perversity in terms of law.
18. Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case and the law of the subject, appeal deserves to fail and is dismissed accordingly.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) (DEVNARAYAN MI  JUDGE JUDGE  AR Ravi Kol vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43238237/
